credentials: PHD 2003 Univ degli Studi di Milano
name: Elena Donghia

ratings.comment: Had an "attendance" grade but only required like 70% of classes attended and halfway through she was just like "actually it doesn't even matter." She explains material simply and loves engaging directly with the students. Minimal HW that is given right before exams as basically a "mock" exam.

Professor Elena is a kind lecturer. Attendance is not really mandatory. Pretty interesting content with very basic math involved. Tests and midterms are open book and pretty easy. Can drop the final if your midterm scores are good. A great and easy way to fulfill Physical Science requirement.

- This course was made ridiculously easy this semester. Ridiculously easy. I expect the A rate to be well over 90%. Every single assignment/quiz/exam was in effect open everything. The grades reflected this as the median was an A on virtually all assignments. Lectures were interesting for those intrigued by the subject.

Elena is very kind and positive in lecture. I got very lucky with a great TA but i could imagine the class being a lot harder if given a bad one. You are allowed to drop 1 test and 1 quiz and there is an extra credit opportunity. Do with that what you will.
This class is simply not a good class to take, but she is nice. I would look elsewhere for a physical science credit.

Being a non-astronomy major this class really built my interest in astronomy. I genuinely enjoyed the class and the topics. Professor D'Onghia is a really nice lecturer and her lectures helped me learn all the material really well!

Prof D'Onghia wasn't the best lecturer and I often had to learn large chunks of material myself before the exams. The class has a policy of best 3 out of 4 exams. Lecture attendance is mandatory with questions on TopHat during lectures. There is a textbook, but I never used it. You should go through the class questions and homework before the exam.

Professor D'onghia was very enthusiastic in her lectures which made ASTRO 103 pretty easy to understand. If you do well on the 3 midterms, you don't have to take the final- this policy was something I really liked.

This class is really interesting and she makes the exams all based on the textbook, so if you read and/or go to lecture you should be totally fine! This is a really fun class if you're at all interested in astronomy and if you do well on the midterms you don't need to take the final which is cool.

I personally loved Elena's teaching style. She structured the class so that if you paid attention in lecture and did the homework, then it was easy to succeed. Honestly, most of my peers that disliked her made little to no effort to learn the material, which I do not think is her fault at all. I think she did a phenomenal job and I learned a lot.
The course material from the book is totally different from the exams, but the lectures are just pictures with minimal content. Basically self taught, don't take if you don't have to.

Once you get used to her accent, her lectures are very clear and understandable. Only rarely was I confused at what she is saying. Also, while exams are difficult, you do get to drop your lowest exam score (including the final), so if you screw up you can drop it. It is clear she has a passion for what she is teaching.

An easy class that was made difficult to get an A in due to poorly written test questions.  Reading the text book will help you understand the concepts, but it doesn't necessarily mean you'll do well on the tests because of the lack of clarity.

This class is made way too difficult for a 103 level.  The multiple choice tests are very detailed.  I highly recommend not taking this class.  Take any different science class.  When I would e-mail the Professor for help she seem uninterested in helping me and just tell me to study harder.  TA's not helpful either.
D'onghia is awesome. Shes kinda iffy on the clarity at first, but once her accent she's awesome. Easy class, very interesting.

If you like watching anything related to The Universe on the Science Channel, this is the class for you! Super nice, accent does get in the way sometimes, but she tries to make herself clear. Exams are not difficult (study from slides online), multiple choice, 30ish questions. 6 Homeworks, 3 Quizzes, 2 midterms, 1 final=All Grading. Easy A IMO.
The worst class I've taken at Madison. She makes the science a lot more difficult than it should be. It's very to keep yourself motivated in her class. I don't see how anyone can do well.
